description: Exhaustive AIP compliance evals for the resource-oriented-design skill. One eval per AIP. Each assertion maps to a specific RFC 2119 normative requirement (MUST / MUST NOT / SHOULD / SHOULD NOT) that is structurally observable in a proto definition. Behavioral requirements (server error codes, runtime semantics, token opacity) are excluded — they cannot be verified from the proto alone.
reference_domain: Library API (Publishers → Books) — Google's canonical AIP reference domain. See https://google.aip.dev/

evals.prompt: Define the resource name scheme for a Book resource in a Library API. Books belong to Publishers. Show the proto message definition for Book and the relevant request message fields for a method that acts on a book.
assertions: The Book resource message has a field called `name` of type `string` — MUST: resource name field must be type string and named `name`
The `name` field is the first field in the Book message — SHOULD: first field should be the resource name
The `name` field on the Book resource is NOT called anything other than `name` — MUST NOT: fields must not be called `name` except for the resource name of that specific resource
Collection identifiers are the plural form of the noun: `books` not `book`, `publishers` not `publisher` — MUST: collection identifiers must be plural
Collection identifiers begin with a lowercase letter and contain only ASCII letters and numbers, matching /[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*/ — MUST
Collection identifiers are in camelCase — MUST
Collection identifiers are concise American English terms — MUST
Resource name segments alternate collection identifier and resource ID: `publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}` — SHOULD: should usually alternate
Resource names use `/` to separate segments — no other separator — MUST
Non-terminal name segments do NOT contain a `/` character — MUST NOT
Resource IDs do NOT use upper-case letters — SHOULD NOT
All resource ID fields exposed separately (e.g., `book_id`) are of type `string`, not integer — SHOULD: all ID fields should be strings
If a separate resource ID field (e.g., `book_id`) is exposed, it is annotated `OUTPUT_ONLY` — MUST
The Book resource message has a `(google.api.resource)` annotation — SHOULD
In request messages acting on an existing book (Get, Update, Delete), the first field is `string name` — MUST: action request field must be type string and called `name`
In List-style request messages, the first field is `string parent` of type `string` — SHOULD
The `name` field in action request messages is annotated with `(google.api.resource_reference)` referencing the Book resource type — SHOULD
The `parent` field in collection request messages is annotated with `(google.api.resource_reference)` referencing the parent resource type — SHOULD
Fields are NOT named `parent` except to represent a resource's parent collection — SHOULD NOT
The Book resource does NOT expose tuples, self-links, or other forms of resource identification — only the `name` string field identifies the resource — MUST NOT (AIP-122)
If a system-generated unique ID field (`uid`) is present on the resource, it is annotated `OUTPUT_ONLY` — MUST (AIP-122)
Collection identifiers within a single resource name pattern are unique — e.g., `people/{person}/people/{person2}` is invalid — MUST (AIP-122)
Fields that reference another resource use that resource message's name in snake_case — e.g., a field referencing `Publisher` is named `publisher`, not `publisherId` — SHOULD (AIP-122)
Fields referencing another resource do NOT use a `_name` suffix unless the field would be ambiguous without it — e.g., `publisher` not `publisher_name` — SHOULD NOT (AIP-122)
Fields referencing another resource are of type `string` (holding the resource name), NOT of the message type that implements the resource — SHOULD NOT (AIP-122)

evals.prompt: Define resource type annotations for Book and Publisher resources in a Library API using `google.api.resource`. The service name is `library.googleapis.com`.
assertions: Each resource has a `(google.api.resource)` annotation with a `type` field — MUST: API must define a resource type for each resource
The `type` value follows the pattern `{ServiceName}/{Type}` — e.g., `library.googleapis.com/Book` — MUST
The type name (after the `/`) starts with an uppercase letter — MUST
The type name uses PascalCase / UpperCamelCase — MUST
The type name is the singular form of the noun: `Book` not `Books` — MUST
The type name contains only alphanumeric characters — MUST
The `(google.api.resource)` annotation has a `pattern` field — e.g., `publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}` — MUST: patterns must correspond to the resource name
Pattern variables (segments within braces) use snake_case — e.g., `{book}`, not `{bookId}` or `{bookID}` — MUST
Pattern variables conform to `[a-z][_a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9]` format — MUST
Pattern variables do NOT use an `_id` suffix — `{book}` not `{book_id}` — MUST NOT
Pattern variables are unique within any given pattern — e.g., `publishers/{publisher}/books/{publisher}` would be invalid — MUST
Pattern variables are the singular form of the resource type — e.g., `{book}` for a Book resource — MUST
Pattern collection identifier segments match the plural of the resource — `books` in `publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}` — MUST
The `singular` value in the resource annotation is lower camelCase of the type — e.g., `book` — MUST
The `plural` value in the resource annotation is lower camelCase plural — e.g., `books` — MUST
If multiple patterns are defined, they are mutually unique (identical structure once resource ID segments are removed) — MUST
Existing patterns are NOT removed or re-ordered if new patterns are added — MUST NOT: breaks client library backward compatibility

evals.prompt: Design a GetBook RPC for a Library API. Books have the resource name pattern `publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}`. Include the full proto RPC definition, request message, and HTTP annotation.
assertions: The RPC name begins with `Get` — e.g., `GetBook` — MUST
The request message name matches the RPC name with a `Request` suffix — e.g., `GetBookRequest` — MUST
The response message is the resource itself (`Book`), NOT a `GetBookResponse` wrapper message — MUST
The `google.api.http` annotation specifies HTTP verb `GET` — MUST
The `google.api.http` annotation does NOT have a `body` key — MUST NOT
The request message has a field for the resource name — MUST: a resource name field must be included
The resource name field has a `(google.api.resource_reference)` annotation identifying the resource type it references — MUST
The request message has NO other required fields — only the name field may be annotated REQUIRED — MUST NOT: must not contain any other required fields
The RPC name suffix is the singular form of the resource: `GetBook` not `GetBooks` — SHOULD
The resource name field is of type `string` and is called `name` — SHOULD: should be called `name`
The `name` field has `(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED` — SHOULD
The URI path contains a variable corresponding to the `name` field — e.g., `publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}` — SHOULD
The `name` field is the only variable in the URI path — SHOULD
All remaining request fields map to URI query parameters — SHOULD
There is exactly one `(google.api.method_signature)` annotation with value `"name"` — SHOULD
The comment on the `name` field documents the resource pattern — e.g., `// Format: publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}` — SHOULD
The request message does NOT contain other optional fields except those described in AIP-131 or another AIP — SHOULD NOT

evals.prompt: Design a ListBooks RPC for a Library API. Books belong to Publishers (pattern: `publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}`). Include pagination (AIP-158) and a filter field (AIP-160). Include the full proto RPC, request message, response message, and HTTP annotation.
assertions: The RPC name begins with `List` — e.g., `ListBooks` — MUST (AIP-132)
The request message name matches the RPC name with a `Request` suffix — e.g., `ListBooksRequest` — MUST (AIP-132)
The response message name matches the RPC name with a `Response` suffix — e.g., `ListBooksResponse` — MUST (AIP-132)
The `google.api.http` annotation specifies HTTP verb `GET` — MUST (AIP-132)
The `google.api.http` annotation does NOT have a `body` key — MUST (AIP-132)
The collection identifier in the URI path is a literal string — e.g., `books` — not a variable — MUST (AIP-132)
The request message has a `parent` field — books are not a top-level resource — MUST (AIP-132)
The `parent` field has a `(google.api.resource_reference)` annotation identifying the parent resource type — MUST (AIP-132)
The RPC name suffix is the plural form of the resource: `ListBooks` not `ListBook` — SHOULD (AIP-132)
The `parent` field is called `parent` — SHOULD (AIP-132)
The `parent` field has `(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED` — SHOULD (AIP-132)
The URI maps to the collection — e.g., `publishers/{publisher}/books` — SHOULD (AIP-132)
The `parent` field is the only variable in the URI path — SHOULD (AIP-132)
All remaining fields map to URI query parameters — SHOULD (AIP-132)
There is exactly one `(google.api.method_signature)` annotation with value `"parent"` — SHOULD (AIP-132)
The response message has a repeated `Book` field as the first field with field number 1 — SHOULD (AIP-132): results field should be first at field number 1
The request message has an `int32 page_size` field — MUST (AIP-132): page_size and page_token must be included on list requests
The request message has a `string page_token` field — MUST (AIP-132)
The `page_size` field is NOT marked as required — MUST NOT (AIP-158)
The `page_token` field is NOT marked as required — MUST NOT (AIP-158)
The response message has a `string next_page_token` field — MUST (AIP-132): next_page_token must be included on all list response messages
The response message does NOT include any other repeated fields besides the `Book` results field — SHOULD NOT (AIP-132)
The ListBooks RPC does NOT use a streaming return type — `stream ListBooksResponse` would violate this — MUST NOT (AIP-158)
The request message does NOT contain other optional fields except those described in AIP-132 or another AIP — SHOULD NOT (AIP-132)
The request message has exactly one `string filter` field — SHOULD (AIP-160): when providing filtering, request should have exactly one `filter` field
The `filter` field is NOT marked as required — (AIP-160)

evals.prompt: Design a CreateBook RPC for a Library API. Books belong to Publishers. Include the full proto RPC definition, request message, and HTTP annotation.
assertions: The RPC name begins with `Create` — e.g., `CreateBook` — MUST
The request message name matches the RPC name with a `Request` suffix — e.g., `CreateBookRequest` — MUST
The response message is the resource itself (`Book`), NOT a `CreateBookResponse` wrapper — MUST
The `google.api.http` annotation specifies HTTP verb `POST` — MUST
The `google.api.http` annotation has a `body` key that maps to the resource field — e.g., `body: "book"` — MUST
The collection identifier in the URI path is a literal string — e.g., `books` — MUST
The request message has a `parent` field — books are not a top-level resource — MUST
The `parent` field has a `(google.api.resource_reference)` annotation identifying the parent type — MUST
The request message has a resource field of type `Book` — e.g., `Book book` — MUST
The `book_id` field, if present, is on the request message, NOT on the Book resource itself — MUST
The request message has NO other required fields beyond `parent`, the resource field, and optionally `book_id` — MUST NOT
The RPC name suffix is the singular form of the resource: `CreateBook` — SHOULD
The `parent` field is called `parent` — SHOULD
The `parent` field has `(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED` — SHOULD
The URI path maps to the collection — e.g., `publishers/{publisher}/books` — SHOULD
The `parent` field is the only variable in the URI path — SHOULD
A `book_id` field of type `string` exists on the request message — SHOULD (management plane)
There is exactly one `(google.api.method_signature)` annotation — SHOULD
The `name` field on the `Book` resource is annotated `OUTPUT_ONLY` — the server assigns it; it MUST be ignored on creation — MUST
The request message does NOT contain other optional fields except those described in AIP-133 or another AIP — SHOULD NOT
If the CreateBook RPC is long-running, the response message is `google.longrunning.Operation` (not `Book` directly) — MUST (AIP-133)
If using a long-running create, the `google.longrunning.operation_info` annotation specifies both `response_type` (the resource type) and `metadata_type` — MUST (AIP-133)

evals.prompt: Design an UpdateBook RPC for a Library API supporting partial resource update. Include the full proto RPC definition, request message, and HTTP annotation.
assertions: The RPC name begins with `Update` — e.g., `UpdateBook` — MUST
The request message name matches the RPC name with a `Request` suffix — e.g., `UpdateBookRequest` — MUST
The response message is the resource itself (`Book`), NOT an `UpdateBookResponse` wrapper — MUST
The `google.api.http` annotation has a `body` key that maps to the resource field — e.g., `body: "book"` — MUST
The request message has a resource field of type `Book` — e.g., `Book book` — MUST
The `Book` resource message has a `name` field — MUST: name field must be included in the resource
The `name` field on the resource has a `(google.api.resource_reference)` annotation identifying the resource type — MUST
An `update_mask` field of type `google.protobuf.FieldMask` is present in the request message — MUST
The `update_mask` field is called `update_mask` — MUST
The `update_mask` field is NOT required — it is optional — MUST: update_mask must be optional
The request message has NO other required fields besides the resource field — MUST NOT
The HTTP verb is NOT `PUT` — SHOULD NOT: strongly discouraged; adding new fields becomes a breaking change
The `google.api.http` annotation specifies HTTP verb `PATCH` — SHOULD
The resource's `name` field maps to the URI path — e.g., `patch: "{book.name=publishers/*/books/*}"` — SHOULD
`{resource}.name` is the only variable in the URI path — SHOULD
There is exactly one `(google.api.method_signature)` annotation with value `"book,update_mask"` — SHOULD
The resource field in the request is annotated `(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED` — SHOULD
The `name` field within the resource is called `name` — SHOULD
State fields (server-managed state, not user-settable) are NOT directly writable via the update request — MUST NOT
The request message does NOT contain other optional fields except those described in AIP-134 or another AIP — SHOULD NOT
If the UpdateBook RPC is long-running, the response message is `google.longrunning.Operation` (not `Book` directly) — MUST (AIP-134)
If using a long-running update, the `google.longrunning.operation_info` annotation specifies both `response_type` (the resource type) and `metadata_type` — MUST (AIP-134)

evals.prompt: Design a DeleteBook RPC for a Library API. Include the full proto RPC definition, request message, and HTTP annotation.
assertions: The RPC name begins with `Delete` — e.g., `DeleteBook` — MUST
The request message name matches the RPC name with a `Request` suffix — e.g., `DeleteBookRequest` — MUST
The `google.api.http` annotation specifies HTTP verb `DELETE` — MUST
The `google.api.http` annotation does NOT have a `body` key — MUST NOT
The request message has a `name` field of type `string` — MUST
The `name` field has a `(google.api.resource_reference)` annotation identifying the resource type — MUST
The request message has NO other required fields — MUST NOT: must not contain any other required fields
The RPC name suffix is the singular form of the resource: `DeleteBook` not `DeleteBooks` — SHOULD
The response message is `google.protobuf.Empty` for a hard delete — SHOULD
The `name` field is called `name` — SHOULD
The `name` field has `(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED` — SHOULD
The `name` field maps to the URI path — SHOULD
The `name` field is the only variable in the URI path — SHOULD
All remaining fields map to URI query parameters — SHOULD
There is exactly one `(google.api.method_signature)` annotation with value `"name"` — SHOULD
The comment on the `name` field documents the resource pattern — SHOULD
The request message does NOT contain other optional fields except those described in AIP-135 or another AIP — SHOULD NOT
If the DeleteBook RPC is long-running, the response message is `google.longrunning.Operation` (not `google.protobuf.Empty` directly) — MUST (AIP-135)
If using a long-running delete, the `google.longrunning.operation_info` annotation specifies both `response_type` and `metadata_type` — MUST (AIP-135)

evals.prompt: Design an ArchiveBook custom method for a Library API. Archiving a book mutates its state (marks it as archived). It operates on a specific book resource. Include the full proto RPC definition, request message, response message, and HTTP annotation.
assertions: The HTTP method in the `google.api.http` annotation is `POST` — MUST: POST must be used when the method has side effects or mutates resources
The URI uses a `:` character followed by the custom verb — e.g., `/publishers/{publisher}/books/{book}:archive` — MUST
The verb in the URI matches the verb portion of the RPC name in camelCase — e.g., RPC `ArchiveBook` → URI verb `archive` — MUST
The RPC operates on a resource; the resource name parameter is called `name` — MUST: parameter for resource name must be called `name`
The `name` field is the only variable in the URI path — MUST: must be the only variable for resource-based custom methods
The RPC name does NOT contain prepositions — no `ArchiveForBook`, `ArchiveWithTag`, etc. — MUST NOT
The RPC name does NOT include the term `Async` — MUST NOT
The verb portion of the RPC name does NOT match a standard method verb: not Get, List, Create, Update, or Delete — SHOULD NOT
The RPC name is a verb followed by a noun — e.g., `ArchiveBook` — SHOULD
The `body` clause in the `google.api.http` annotation is `"*"` — SHOULD (for POST custom methods)
The request message matches the RPC name with a `Request` suffix — e.g., `ArchiveBookRequest` — SHOULD
The response message matches the RPC name with a `Response` suffix — e.g., `ArchiveBookResponse` — or is the resource itself — SHOULD
If the custom method only retrieves data or resource state (no side effects), the HTTP method is `GET` not `POST` — MUST (AIP-136)

If the custom method operates on a collection (not a single resource) and the collection's resource has a parent, the parent parameter is called `parent` and is the only variable in the URI path — MUST (AIP-136)
If the custom method operates on a collection, the collection key in the URI is a literal string (not a variable) — MUST (AIP-136)
If the custom method is stateless and involves billing, the HTTP method is `POST` — MUST (AIP-136)
